Report an object's type or unit

Source: R/var-type.R
var_type.Rd

Inspect an object's type and measurement metadata:

  • var_type(): Describe the object's storage type or class, optionally using an abbreviation.

  • var_unit(): Report the measurement or duration unit, or NA_character_ when the object has no unit.

Usage

var_type(x, abbr = FALSE)

var_unit(x)

Arguments

x

An object.

abbr

For var_type(), if TRUE, return an abbreviated type. Defaults to FALSE: expand known abbreviations and use full class names for default class abbreviations. Custom display labels are preserved.

Value

  • var_type(): One character string describing the type, including "units" for measured vectors in either abbreviation mode.

  • var_unit(): The unit string for measured or duration vectors, including empty or all-missing measured vectors, or NA_character_ when no unit is available.

Details

Comparison with other type inspectors

var_type() gives one readable label per object, useful for column audits with vapply(data, var_type, character(1)) or dplyr::summarise(data, dplyr::across(dplyr::everything(), var_type)). It combines storage and class information in a display label:

  • typeof() reports the internal storage type. Factors are "integer", while ordinary double vectors, POSIXct date-times and double-backed haven-labelled vectors are all "double". var_type() distinguishes "factor", "double", "datetime" and "double+label".

  • class() reports the class names used for method dispatch and may return several strings, such as c("ordered", "factor"). var_type() reduces this to one label, "ordered". Use class() to inspect the full class vector and inherits() to test class membership in program logic.

  • mode() reports a broader category: both integer and double vectors have mode "numeric". var_type() keeps that storage distinction.

  • utils::str() displays structure and example values. var_type() returns a character string that can be collected into an audit table.

  • pillar::type_sum() supplies compact display labels for classed objects. var_type() builds on those labels, expands recognized abbreviations by default, marks haven value labels and omits container dimensions.

Custom classes can provide a pillar::type_sum() method to control their display label without changes to var_type().

Use var_type() for reporting; use storage or class inspectors when exact R type information is needed. Its display label does not retain the full class hierarchy, attributes or structure.

Type and unit metadata

Types describe storage and class metadata, not the observed values: empty and all-missing vectors retain their type. Known scalar abbreviations expand exactly, including int64 to integer64. Haven-labelled vectors append +lbl in abbreviation mode and +label otherwise.

Plain matrices and arrays retain their element-type description, and data frames retain their container name without dimensions. Other classed objects use their pillar type description. With abbr = FALSE, a default class-name abbreviation is replaced by the full primary class name, for example "dgCMatrix" for a sparse matrix of that class. Registered or inherited display methods and explicit pillar labels take precedence. Custom labels, including punctuation and structured descriptions such as I<int> and list<int>, are preserved in both modes. An empty or missing custom description falls back to the first class name; errors in custom methods are propagated. A numeric-looking type description does not imply support for numeric summaries.

var_unit() reads actual units/difftime metadata (including hms times), and retains custom unit methods for classes describing themselves as units, drtn or time. Other objects return NA_character_.

See also

Other inspection functions: browse(), codebook(), misstable(), names, variables()

Examples

var_type(1:10)
#> [1] "integer"

var_type(1:10, abbr = TRUE)
#> [1] "int"

var_type(letters)
#> [1] "character"

# Compare storage, dispatch classes and readable type labels
objects <- list(
  score = 1.5,
  grade = ordered(c("low", "high"), levels = c("low", "high")),
  recorded = as.POSIXct("2026-01-01", tz = "UTC"),
  answer = haven::labelled(c(1, 2), labels = c(Yes = 1, No = 2))
)

lapply(objects, function(x) {
  tibble::tibble(
    typeof = typeof(x),
    class = paste(class(x), collapse = ", "),
    var_type = var_type(x)
  )
}) |>
  dplyr::bind_rows(.id = "variable")
#> # A tibble: 4 × 4
#>   variable typeof  class                              var_type    
#>   <chr>    <chr>   <chr>                              <chr>       
#> 1 score    double  numeric                            double      
#> 2 grade    integer ordered, factor                    ordered     
#> 3 recorded double  POSIXct, POSIXt                    datetime    
#> 4 answer   double  haven_labelled, vctrs_vctr, double double+label

# Type and unit describe different properties of the same object
elapsed <- as.difftime(c(1, 2, 3), units = "hours")
elapsed
#> Time differences in hours
#> [1] 1 2 3

var_type(elapsed)
#> [1] "duration"

var_unit(elapsed)
#> [1] "hours"
